en: The Sūtra on the Teaching and Transformation of Hell Beings Concerning the Retribution for Sinful Karmas, spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Anxi Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...

The great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and their retinues of Śrāvakas were present together; likewise, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, as well as devas, nāgas, spirits, and others, had all assembled.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Now there are various kinds of beings—those in the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, slaves, the poor and the wealthy, the noble and the lowly. We only pray that the World-Honored One will fully expound the Dharma for us!”

If there are sentient beings who hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, it is like a child finding its mother, like a sick person finding a physician, like a weak person finding food, or like one in darkness finding a lamp; the World-Honored One’s preaching of the Dharma to benefit sentient beings is likewise so.

At that time, the World-Honored One, observing that the moment had arrived and seeing how earnestly this bodhisattva entreated him, immediately emitted a ray of light from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows, illuminating the world—the hells were stilled, and those in suffering found peace.
At that time, all sentient beings undergoing retribution for their offenses, following the Buddha’s radiance, came to where the Buddha was;
they circumambulated the Buddha seven times, prostrated before him,
and entreated the World-Honored One to expound the transformative teachings of the Way, so that these sentient beings might attain liberation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa acted as an instigator for the sake of all sentient beings and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
There are now sentient beings undergoing punishment who are being crushed by pestles and chopped by the hell-wardens, from their heads down to their feet and even to the crown of their heads."
Once he had finished beheading him, a clever wind blew him back to life, and he beheaded him again.
"What crime has caused this?
the Buddha asked.

"In a previous life, I failed to have faith in the Triple Gem, was unfilial toward my parents, and as a butcher and executioner, I slaughtered and dismembered living beings; therefore, I have incurred this retribution."

"Second, there are further sentient beings whose bodies are numb and paralyzed; their eyebrows and beards fall out, and their entire bodies are festering and ulcerated. Birds perch upon them and deer lie down beside them, as human tracks are forever severed. They defile their own kin, whom people do not wish to behold; this is called leprosy.
"By what offenses was this caused?

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, because you did not believe in the Triple Gem, were unfilial toward your parents, destroyed stupas and monasteries, stripped the robes from practitioners of the Way, slew and shot sages and saints, and harmed your teachers and elders; because you were constantly devoid of reciprocity, turned your back on kindness and forgot righteousness, always acted with negligence, and committed lewd acts without avoiding distinctions of high and low, you have incurred this retribution."

"Third, there are further sentient beings whose bodies are large and tall, yet they are deaf and dull-witted, lacking feet and crawling on their bellies. They subsist solely by eating earth to sustain their lives, and are bitten and eaten by various small insects; they constantly undergo this suffering, which is unbearable."
"By what offense was this caused?

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, he sat in judgment over others while acting for his own selfish ends; he did not believe in good words or virtuous speech, was unfilial toward his parents, and acted rebelliously against his sovereign."

Or they may serve as sovereigns, high ministers, governors of the four frontiers, regional lords, magistrates of provinces and commanderies, or officials and military inspectors; relying on their power and influence, they seize and plunder the property of the people without any sense of propriety, causing the people to suffer in exhaustion and sigh with lamentation as they go about their lives.
"Therefore, they incur this retribution.

Fourth, there are further sentient beings whose two eyes are blind and sightless, seeing nothing at all; they may strike against trees or fall into ditches and pits, and after dying, they receive another body in exactly the same manner."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said, "In a previous life,

because you sat in disbelief regarding the retribution of karma and obstructed the light of the Buddha, you sewed together the eyes of hawks, imprisoned sentient beings in cages, and stuffed their heads into leather bags so that they could not see."
"Therefore, they incur this retribution.
Fifth, there are furthermore sentient beings who stammer, are mute, and cannot speak;
if they have something to say, they close their eyes and raise their hands, yet still cannot express themselves clearly."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said, "In a previous life,

you sat in slander against the Triple Gem, disparaged the Holy Path, discussed the merits and faults of others, sought out the shortcomings of men, falsely accused the virtuous, and harbored malice and envy toward the worthy."
"Therefore, they incur this retribution.
Sixth, there are further sentient beings whose bellies are large and their necks are thin, such that they cannot swallow food;
if they do consume anything, it turns into pus and blood."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said,
"In a previous life, you stole food belonging to the Sangha, or you stole and ate from the merit-food provided for a great assembly while remaining in a secluded place."
Being stingy with one's own possessions while coveting only the wealth of others,
and constantly harboring evil intentions by giving people toxic drugs so that their breath is obstructed— therefore,
they incur this retribution.

"Seventh, there are further sentient beings who are constantly subjected by the hell-wardens to being nailed through their hundred joints and bones with glowing iron nails; once the nailing is complete, fire spontaneously arises, burning their bodies until they are entirely scorched and rotted away."
"By what offense was this brought about?
The Buddha said, "In a previous life, he served as an acupuncturist; when he applied needles to people's bodies, he was unable to cure their illnesses."
"By deceiving others to take their wealth, one merely undergoes suffering and causes others distress;
thus, one incurs this retribution.

"The eighth [hell]: furthermore, there are sentient beings who are constantly in cauldrons of boiling water. The ox-headed *ābhangas* impale them with three-pronged iron forks and thrust them into the cauldrons to boil them until they are烂 (làn—putrefied). They are then blown upon to bring them back to life, only to be boiled once more."
"By what offense was this caused?

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, he believed in heterodox and inverted views; he performed sacrifices to ghosts and spirits, slaughtering sentient beings, pouring boiling water over them, plucking their feathers, and boiling them in cauldrons of hot water in measureless quantities."
"Therefore, they incur this retribution.

Ninth, there are further sentient beings who constantly dwell within a city of fire, where hot ashes reach their hearts. All four gates are open; yet whenever they wish to approach one, the gate immediately closes. They run hither and thither, unable to escape, until they are utterly consumed by the flames."
"By what offense was this caused?

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, he sat upon and burned mountains and marshes; he roasted chicken eggs with fire; he burned villages and roads; and he scorched and boiled sentient beings until their bodies were mangled and their skin flayed."
Therefore, they incur this retribution.
"Tenth, furthermore, there are sentient beings who constantly dwell amidst the Snowy Mountains; blown by cold winds, their skin and flesh are torn and split, yet they cannot find death."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said,
"In a previous life, while traveling along a crossroads, he committed robbery and stripped people of their clothing, causing them to die of cold during the winter months."
"Because they were born alive and flayed from cattle and sheep, their pain was unbearable;
thus they have incurred this retribution.

Eleventh, there are further sentient beings who constantly dwell upon mountains of knives and trees of swords; whenever they cast themselves down, they are immediately cut and wounded, their limbs and joints severed and destroyed."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said:

"In a previous life, he made his livelihood by slaughtering; he cooked and harmed sentient beings, cutting, carving, flaying, and tearing them apart until their bones and flesh were separated and their heads and feet scattered. He hung them on high racks and sold them by weight."
"Furthermore, they may be born in places of suspended suffering where sentient beings endure great pain;
thus they incur this retribution.
Twelfth, there are also sentient beings who lack one or more of the five faculties."
"By what offense was this caused?

The Buddha said, "In a previous life, while sitting [at ease], he used flying hawks and running dogs to shoot at birds and beasts; he would sever their heads or their legs, and pluck out the wings of living birds."
"Therefore, they incur this retribution.

"The thirteenth: furthermore, there are sentient beings who are hunchbacked, crippled, or bent over; whose waists and hips are infirm; whose feet are lame and hands are withered, such that they are unable to move about or travel."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said,
"In a previous life, while sitting, you were cruel and exacting toward others, and you drove a stake into the path."
"Or they set up bird-nets and lay out snares and pits to trap and fell sentient beings, causing their heads to be split and their legs to be broken, with injuries of many kinds.
Therefore, they incur this retribution.
"The fourteenth: furthermore, there are sentient beings who are constantly bound by the jailers of hell, shackling their bodies so that they cannot escape."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said, "In a previous life,
you sat by a net to capture living beings, confining them in cages and keeping them there, subjecting them to hunger, exhaustion, and suffering."

Or, having served as a magistrate, a district governor, or a local official, they greedily seized wealth and money, unjustly imprisoning the virtuous and good; these people cried out in resentment and suffering to Heaven, unable to act according to their will.
For this reason, they incur this retribution.
"15. Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are either epileptic, insane, foolish, or idiotic, unable to distinguish between the beautiful and the ugly.
What sin has caused this?"
The Buddha said:

"Because in a previous life he sat and drank wine until intoxicated and deranged, committing thirty-six transgressions, he subsequently obtained a deluded body like that of a drunkard, unable to recognize the honorable from the lowly or distinguish the beautiful from the ugly."

For eighty thousand kalpas, he fell into the Boiling Excrement Hell, where hell-wardens hacked and mangled him; seeking death, he could not find it, and seeking life, he could not find it. Exhausted in every way and driven to the utmost limit, he suffered through the long night for the transgression of his greed for wine.
Having finished undergoing these punishments, they finally obtain human form, yet they are humpbacked, crippled, or lame, and are detested and envied by others;
wherever they go they encounter misfortunes, and there is never a time of happiness.
"Because of the transgression of excessive drinking, they have incurred this retribution.
"Sixteenth, there are further sentient beings whose bodies are very small, yet their male organs are exceedingly large;
when they pull them, their bodies become exhausted, yet they continue to draw them forward."
"Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, these [actions] have become an impediment.
By what offense has this been caused?
The Buddha said:
"In a former life, while engaged in business and trade, he praised his own goods and disparaged the wealth of others;
he cheated people by shaking the scales and manipulating the weights, and by tampering with the measures from front to back."
Therefore, they incur this retribution.
"Seventeenth, there are further sentient beings who lack the male organ and possess the body of a eunuch, unable to take a wife."
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said, "In a previous life,
he sat upon joyful elephants, horses, oxen, sheep, pigs, and dogs in incalculable numbers, causing these sentient beings unbearable pain until they died and then revived."
"Therefore, they incur this retribution.
"The eighteenth: furthermore, there are sentient beings who, from birth until old age, have no sons and remain solitary and alone.
What offense leads to this?"
The Buddha said:
"In a previous life, he was violent and wicked toward others and did not believe in the retribution of sin and merit.

When the various birds were laying eggs, he would carry jars and vessels along the banks of great waters to seek out and collect the eggs of swans, cranes, parrots, geese, and wild ducks; he would then carry them back home to boil and eat."
Various birds, having lost their young, wail with cries of rending grief until blood flows from their eyes;
thus they incur this retribution.

"Nineteenth, furthermore, there are sentient beings who, from childhood, have been orphaned and destitute, lacking parents and brothers, serving as laborers for others to eke out a living through toil and hardship."
Having grown up and reached adulthood, he was suddenly beset by calamities and misfortunes; bound by the local authorities, he was imprisoned and confined in a jail.
With no one to bring him food or sustenance, he suffered from hunger, destitution, and hardship, having no one to whom he could turn for help.
"By what offense was this caused?
The Buddha said:

"In a previous life, you delighted in capturing and gathering eagles, vultures, hawks, falcons, bears, brown bears, tigers, and leopards; you imprisoned them with shackles and kept them as livestock. You isolated these sentient beings, causing their parents and brothers to be in constant grief and anxiety. They cried out with heart-rending lamentation, their sorrow moving the hearts of all people."
"Unable to make offerings, they are constantly tormented by hunger; their bones stand out against skin that clings to them, and though they seek death, they cannot find it.

Thus they incur this retribution. "The twentieth: furthermore, there are sentient beings whose forms are exceedingly ugly; their bodies are black as lacquer, their two eyes are blue, and both their heads and cheeks are swollen. Their faces are pockmarked, their noses are flat, their eyes are yellowish-red, and their teeth are sparse and missing. Their breath is foul and putrid; they are short and stunted, with boils and swellings, large bellies, and protruding hips. Their legs are twisted and crooked, their spines are hunched, and their ribs stick out. They wear clothes wastefully and eat voraciously; various evils such as malignant sores with pus and blood, dropsy, consumption, scabies, leprosy, carbuncles, and abscesses all gather upon their bodies."
Though they may attach themselves closely to others, those others pay them no heed;
if others commit offenses, they are falsely implicated in their calamities;
they shall never see the Buddha, never hear the Dharma, and never recognize the Sangha.
"By what offense was this caused? The Buddha said:

"In a previous life, when he was a son, he was unfilial toward his parents; as a minister, he was disloyal to his sovereign; as a ruler, he was disrespectful to his subordinates; among friends, he was not faithful; in his village community, he did not respect the order of seniority; and at court, he did not honor the rank of office."
Driven by their destinies, they act with perverted minds and lack any sense of restraint;
they do not believe in the Triple Gem, kill their sovereigns, and harm their teachers;
they invade nations and plunder the people, besiege cities and destroy fortresses, and commit thefts and robberies—such evil karmas are manifold.

They praise themselves and disparage others; they oppress the orphaned and the elderly; they slander the worthy and the holy; they treat their elders with contempt; and they deceive those of low station.
They have committed every kind of sinful deed.
"Because the retribution for the accumulation of all evils has gathered, we have incurred this punishment.

At that time, when all the sentient beings undergoing punishment heard the Buddha speak these words, their lamentations shook the earth and their tears fell like rain. They addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We only pray that the World-Honored One will dwell long and preach the Dharma, so that we and our kind may attain liberation!"
The Buddha said:
“If I were to remain for a long time, those of meager virtue would not plant roots of goodness; thinking that I am always present, they would not contemplate impermanence.
Good son!...”
It is like a child whose mother is always by his side; he does not conceive the thought that she is difficult to encounter.
But if the mother were to depart, he would immediately give rise to a heart of longing, thirsting for her presence and yearning for her.
Only when the mother returns does he feel joy.
Good son! I now do likewise;
knowing the karmic conditions of good and evil for all sentient beings, and the excellence or inferiority of the retributions they receive, I therefore enter parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses for the sake of all those sentient beings undergoing retribution:
"The flowing water is never constantly full; The blazing fire does not burn for long.
The rising sun sets in an instant; The full moon wanes once again."
"For those who are honored, illustrious, and noble, impermanence surpasses even this;
one should reflect and strive with diligent vigor, prostrating before the Unsurpassed Honored One.
When the World-Honored One had spoken these verses, the sentient beings undergoing retribution addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
By practicing what wholesome conduct can one escape from this suffering?
The Buddha said:
"One should diligently practice filial piety and obedience toward one's parents, respectfully serve one's teachers and elders, and take refuge in and honor the Triple Gem;

one should diligently practice generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; cultivate loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; treat enemies and kin with equality, regarding them as no different from oneself;
do not deceive the orphaned or the elderly, and do not look down upon those of low station, protecting others as one protects oneself."
"If you are able to practice in this manner, you will have already repaid the Buddha's kindness and shall forever be free from all suffering.

When this sutra had been spoken, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas immediately attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas immediately attained the six supernormal powers, the three insights, and were endowed with the eight liberations; and some attained the purity of the Dharma-eye.

"If there are sentient beings who hear this sutra, they shall not fall into the three miserable realms or the eight difficult conditions; the hells shall find rest, and their suffering shall be pacified.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:
"What should this sutra be named?"
"How should it be upheld?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa:
"Good son!..."

This sutra is titled "The Sutra on the Teaching and Transformation of Hell through the Retribution of Sinful Karma"; you should uphold it and cause it to be widely disseminated, for its merit shall be immeasurable!
The great assembly of devas, having heard this sutra, rejoiced; they prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground, paid homage, and practiced accordingly.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Retribution of Sinful Karma and the Instruction of Those in Hell.
